cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: inverse hyperbolic tangent of 0.76159416
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 1.00000001. Independently verified in Python: math.atanh(0.76159416) = 1.0000000096297197 = 0.5*ln(1.76159416/0.23840584) -> 1.00000001 at 8 dp (the argument is tanh(1) rounded to 8 dp, hence the result is 1 plus a small residue rather than exactly 1)

cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: inverse hyperbolic tangent of -0.1
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as -0.100335348. Independently verified in Python: math.atanh(-0.1) = -0.10033534773107558 -> -0.100335348 at 9 dp

cases.description: An argument of exactly 1 is excluded by the documented open interval
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "Number must be between -1 and 1 (excluding -1 and 1)"; at 1 the inverse hyperbolic tangent diverges, which is Excel's documented #NUM! case
#VALUE! is Excel's documented error for an argument of the wrong type; the ACOT page states it explicitly for this inverse-hyperbolic family
